en.name: Stack CRM

en.lead: Pipeline, accounts, contacts, tasks, and document originals on your OnlyOffice / Postgres plane — plus a file data plane (S3, SMB, SSH) so desks, agents, and backups share one corpus without SaaS egress.

en.overview: Stack CRM is the structured office system of record for sovereign installs: deals and contacts live next to document originals in OnlyOffice. Same IdP and observability plane as Chat and Meet — adding modules later is wiring, not a re-platform.

en.name: Stack Chat
en.lead: Channels, threads, DMs, voice notes, and file sharing — end-to-end encrypted with keys you hold. Native agent bots with long-term memory, STT/TTS, and optional call join — still on your homeserver.
en.overview: Stack Chat is the collaboration spine of the suite. Search, files, and presence stay on infrastructure you control. Positive feedback can be written back into long-term memory. Native clients cover desk and mobile so field and office share one secure plane.

en.name: Observing
en.tag: Part of Stack Platform · monitoring · edge · DNS · QEMU
en.lead: Observing is the ops half of Stack Platform: Grafana / Prometheus / Loki for the fleet, Nginx Proxy Manager for service front-doors and your own DNS names, ddclient when the WAN IP moves — plus finely tuned QEMU for legacy servers you cannot rewrite yet.
replaces: Ad-hoc port forwards / ISP DDNS gadgets
en.overview: Observing is day-2 ops inside Stack Platform. Metrics and logs land in one Grafana/Prometheus/Loki plane; Alertmanager fans out to Matrix. In front of every module sits Nginx Proxy Manager: TLS, host-based routing, and your own DNS names (produktor.io or customer zones) instead of raw ports. On dynamic WAN links, ddclient (or equivalent) keeps A/AAAA records fresh so cutovers and demos keep working after DHCP renumbering — that DNS + proxy pair is part of standard setup, not an afterthought. Where Windows / old Linux appliances still matter, we virtualize them under QEMU/KVM with explicit CPU, disk, and network profiles, scheduled backups, and Grafana visibility — so legacy and modern compose stacks share one site without surprise coupling.
